name: Pitts Special (S-1 / S-2)
manufacturer: Pitts Aerospace / Christen Industries / Aviat Aircraft (Curtis Pitts design)
summary: Tiny, ultra-agile aerobatic biplane that has dominated competition aerobatics since the 1960s; the single-seat S-1 and two-seat S-2 share one basic layout.

wings: Very short-span staggered biplane with a single bay of struts and bracing wires
Ailerons on both upper and lower wings on later models
engines: Cowled horizontally opposed Lycoming, flat-four in the S-1 and S-2A, flat-six in the S-2B/S-2C/S-2S
Short nose with a two- or three-blade prop
fuselage: Very short, stubby fuselage with cockpit(s) set far back
Single open cockpit (S-1) or two tandem open cockpits (S-2)
Fixed tailwheel gear with short main legs
tail: Compact tail close behind the wings with a tall, rounded rudder

tellTales: Tiny, stubby biplane with very short wings and a very short fuselage
Staggered wings joined by a single bay of struts, with cockpit(s) set far back
Cowled flat engine with a short nose and an open cockpit

confusedWith.howToTell: The Stearman is a much larger biplane with an uncowled radial engine; the Pitts is tiny with a cowled flat engine.
The Great Lakes is a bit bigger with a longer, slimmer fuselage and a swept-back upper wing; the Pitts is stubbier with straight wings.
The Extra is a single-wing monoplane (no second wing) while the Pitts is a biplane.
